pages.text: $(italic)Pruinodendron glaciale.$() A squat, wind-shaped conifer that keeps growing after every other tree has died.

pages.title: Groves
pages.text: From $(bold)Phase 3$(), groves of $(bold)2-4 trees$() take root on cold, open ground in any land. They're rare and far apart; there are no Rimewood forests.$(br2)Groves appear only where it's -20°C or colder.

pages.title: Planting
pages.text: Dirt, dead grass or frozen dirt, with open sky above.$(br2)No sunlight needed, but it grows only at $(bold)-20°C or colder$(). Farming means working in the cold.

pages.title: Growth
pages.text: $(li)About $(bold)25 minutes$() to mature$(li)Or 4-6 bone meal, in the cold only$(li)Warmth pauses it without harm; heaters don't help$(br2)A tree gives about $(bold)8-12 logs$() and 2 saplings. Fortune finds more.

pages.title: Field Note
pages.text: $(italic)Rimewood remains metabolically active at temperatures previously classified as incompatible with forestry. ORSA has revised that classification to 'inconvenient.'$()

pages.title: Rimewood Resin
pages.text: Strip a log or wood with an axe: $(bold)one resin$() per log.$(br2)Resin and sulfur make a $(l:advanced/nether_substitutes)Thermal Binder$(/l).

pages.title: Frostcap Host
pages.text: Most grove trees carry $(bold)Frostcap$() shelves on their sides. Caps grow twice as fast on Rimewood as on snow.$(br2)See $(l:getting_started/frostcap)Frostcap$(/l).
Four planks per log. Works in ordinary wood recipes (no boat), burns as fuel and smelts to charcoal. The planks don't freeze.
